back_translation: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard released him at Ramah, when he had taken him bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being exiled to Babylon.
The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, The LORD your God pronounced this disaster against this place,
and the LORD has brought it about and done just as he said, because you sinned against the LORD and did not obey his voice; so this thing has happened to you.

And now, behold, I free you today from the chains that were on your wrist. If it is good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eye on you to care for you; but if it is wrong in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, stop. See, the whole land is before you; wherever it is good and right in your eyes to go, go there.

While he had not yet turned to go, Nebuzaradan said, Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him among the people, or go wherever it is right in your eyes to go. Then the captain of the guard gave him a ration and a gift and released him.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and dwelt with him among the people who were left in the land.

When all the commanders of the armies that were in the field, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he had put in his charge men, women, and children, and some of the poorest of the land who had not been exiled to Babylon,

they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite—they and their men.

And Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and their men, saying, Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

As for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to us; but you, gather wine, summer fruit, and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken.

Likewise, all the Jews who were in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant for Judah, and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.
Then all the Jews returned from all the places to which they had been banished, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and gathered wine and summer fruit in great abundance.
Now Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies in the field came to Gedaliah at Mizpah,
and said to him, Do you know that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life? But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah, saying, Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know it. Why should he take your life, so that all Judah who have gathered to you would be scattered and the remnant of Judah would perish?
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely about Ishmael.
